description: Material failure modes decomposed. Fatigue (S-N, e-N, fracture mechanics), brittle vs ductile fracture, creep, corrosion (galvanic, pitting, SCC), wear, hydrogen embrittlement, stress concentration factors.

sub_mechanisms.name: endurance_limit_steel
sub_mechanisms.definition: Steel + iron: stress below ~half UTS = infinite life. Aluminum + non-ferrous: no clear limit.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of fatigue design. Steel designed below endurance limit: no fatigue. Non-ferrous: design for finite cycles.

sub_mechanisms.name: S_N_curve_high_cycle
sub_mechanisms.definition: Log-log: stress amplitude vs cycles to failure. Slope on log-log.
sub_mechanisms.why: Engineering fatigue data. Tests at multiple stress levels. Curve drives design.

sub_mechanisms.name: epsilon_N_curve_low_cycle
sub_mechanisms.definition: Strain vs cycles. For high-strain (plastic) cycling. Coffin-Manson.
sub_mechanisms.why: Thermal cycling, high local stress. Solder joints, hot section. Different physics than high-cycle fatigue.

sub_mechanisms.name: stress_concentration_factor
sub_mechanisms.definition: Kt = σ_max/σ_nominal. Geometric features amplify local stress.
sub_mechanisms.why: Holes, notches, fillets. Kt = 3 for circular hole in plate. Fatigue: even higher Kf (fatigue concentration).

sub_mechanisms.name: fracture_toughness_K_IC
sub_mechanisms.definition: Critical stress intensity. K_I = σ√(πa)·Y. K_I ≥ K_IC → fracture.
sub_mechanisms.why: Damage tolerance. Larger crack OR higher stress = fracture. Material property + thickness-dependent.

sub_mechanisms.name: Charpy_impact_test
sub_mechanisms.definition: Notched specimen broken by pendulum. Energy absorbed = impact toughness.
sub_mechanisms.why: Ductile-brittle transition temperature for steel. Liberty ships' transition in cold WWII Atlantic = brittle failures. Critical material property.

sub_mechanisms.name: creep_curve
sub_mechanisms.definition: Primary (decreasing rate), secondary (steady-state), tertiary (accelerating to rupture).
sub_mechanisms.why: High temperature life. Larson-Miller parameter combines T + time. Critical for turbines, pressure vessels.

sub_mechanisms.name: galvanic_corrosion
sub_mechanisms.definition: Two dissimilar metals in electrolyte. Anodic metal corrodes preferentially.
sub_mechanisms.why: Galvanic series predicts. Steel + brass + saltwater → steel corrodes. Sacrificial anodes (zinc, Mg) protect.

sub_mechanisms.name: stress_corrosion_cracking
sub_mechanisms.definition: SCC: simultaneous stress + corrosive environment. Crack propagates faster than corrosion alone.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stainless steel + chloride, brass + ammonia. Catastrophic + sudden. Avoid by material selection or stress relief.

sub_mechanisms.name: hydrogen_embrittlement
sub_mechanisms.definition: Hydrogen diffuses into metal lattice; reduces ductility; causes brittle fracture.
sub_mechanisms.why: High-strength steels, plated parts. Bake-out post-plating mitigates. Catastrophic failures of fasteners + structures.

sub_mechanisms.name: wear_mechanisms
sub_mechanisms.definition: Adhesive, abrasive, fatigue, erosion, corrosive wear. Each different physics.
sub_mechanisms.why: Bearings, gears, cutting tools. Hard surfaces, lubrication, materials selection. Standard engineering concern.

sub_mechanisms.name: Soderberg_Goodman_diagrams
sub_mechanisms.definition: Fatigue design: mean stress vs alternating stress. Safe region bounded by line.
sub_mechanisms.why: Combined static + cyclic loading. Soderberg conservative; Goodman common. Standard shaft + spring design.

derivation_rules.name: stress_concentration_amplifies_fatigue
derivation_rules.why: Cracks initiate at high stress. Round transitions, fillets, eliminate sharp internal corners. Design rules of thumb in modern guidance.

derivation_rules.name: brittle_fracture_catastrophic
if: material is brittle at service temperature
derivation_rules.why: Ductile materials warn by deforming. Brittle: no warning. Concrete, glass, cold steel. Design philosophy: avoid brittle conditions.

derivation_rules.name: galvanic_couples_predicted_by_potential_difference
then: more anodic metal corrodes, more cathodic protected
derivation_rules.why: Galvanic series: Zn, Al anodic; Cu, Au cathodic. Steel between. Pair design intentionally for sacrificial protection or avoid.

derivation_rules.name: creep_dominates_at_T_above_half_melting
derivation_rules.why: Steel at 1000K (700°C): creep critical. At 600K (300°C): negligible. Determines material selection for high-T service.

derivation_rules.name: hydrogen_embrittlement_requires_baking
then: bake-out at 200°C required to remove hydrogen
derivation_rules.why: Plating introduces H. Without bake: delayed brittle failure (hours-days post-plating). Standard process control in aerospace fasteners.
